transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump says he's rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
NPR's Eva Pukach has her reports.
Trump told reporters Saturday that the deal "would not be acceptable."
Iran made the proposal, which also called for resuming negotiations between the U.S.
and Iran at the United Nations General Assembly meetings.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Arachi told reporters Friday that it was a "concrete
seven-day plan" to reopen the Strait.
He said the Strait would be opened on the sixth day, with negotiations on Iran's nuclear
program starting the day after.
The proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding the U.S. and Iran agreed to
in June.
That deal collapsed shortly after due to disputes over the memo's vague wording, including language
related to who would control the Strait.
The U.S. and Iran resumed strikes soon after.
Eva Pukach, NPR News.
A powerful storm is continuing to move along a northeastern coast of the U.S. at this hour.
Some 100,000 people were without power on Saturday, and the storm has led to flight
cancellations and concert postponements.
The National Weather Service is warning that high winds, tides, and heavy rain will continue
through Sunday.
The Baja Peninsula and parts of inland northwest Mexico are preparing for Hurricane Polo.
KJZZ's Nina Kravinsky reports from Hermosillo in Sonora, Mexico.
Officials in the Mexican states of Baja California Sur and Sonora are watching conditions in
the Pacific as Hurricane Polo nears landfall.
The National Weather Service downgraded Polo to a Category 4 hurricane, but warned it remains
a powerful storm.
Polo is predicted to make landfall in Mexico's Baja Peninsula on Monday as a less intense
but still strong hurricane.
The storm has been fluctuating between the Category 4 and Category 5 storm after intensifying
rapidly off of Mexico's Pacific coast.
The U.S. Embassy in Mexico warns travelers to be aware of flooding, mudslides, and road
closures early in the week.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Kravinsky in Hermosillo, Mexico.
CNN is getting a new owner.
Paramount is taking over CNN parent Warner Brothers Discovery, and David Ellison controls
Paramount.
He is also a supporter of President Trump.
Media observers are now looking at what that will mean for CNN's news coverage.
NPR's David Falkenflick has more.
You're probably going to see a pointed within CNN.
Somebody who's willing to do business with the Ellison's doesn't necessarily compromise
their journalistic integrity, but understand what kind of coverage the Ellison's might
be interested in.
You know, you saw at two major publications taken over by Rupert Murdoch, the media magnate
at the Times of London in the 80s, The Wall Street Journal in the late aughts around 2007.
There were such boards created.
And after sort of raising a question here and there, he just kind of ignored and then
overrode them.
That's NPR's David Falkenflick, and this is NPR News.
In Brazil, with just a little over a week left before national elections, the president
has ordered a ban on online betting.
The move the Brazilian leader says is for health and welfare of families who are falling
deeper into debt in the South American country, NPR's Kiri Khan reports.
Online gambling has exploded in Brazil in recent years, and so has personal debt, as
well as gambling addictions and suicides, according to a recent national study.
In signing the banning order, President Luis Anacio Lula da Silva said his decision was
hard and drastic, but necessary.
Lula is locked in a tough reelection campaign with the son of former right wing president
Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio Bolsonaro, who is polling at a statistical tie with Lula for the presidency,
criticized the ban as a "electoral measure."
Brazil's central bank estimates that Brazilians spend nearly $6 billion a month on gambling.
Brazil's soccer clubs, however, say without the advertising from online betting houses,
their clubs could close.
Kiri Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
Russian attacks are continuing on Ukraine this weekend.
Officials say two women were killed in Zaporizhia while two other people were killed in Sumi.
The Russian attacks included missiles, glide bombs, and drones.
In Russia, Ukrainian drone strikes on several oil refineries killed three people.
A manhunt is underway in St. Vincent and the Grenadines this weekend after a shooting there
that killed four people.
Four others were injured, with two of them still hospitalized.
No arrests were made, and the motive for the shooting is unclear, but authorities have
been struggling to stop gang violence in that Caribbean island nation.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump rejects Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear negotiations
Powerful storm moves along northeastern U.S. coast, leaving 100,000 without power, causing flight cancellations
Hurricane Polo downgraded to Category 4, expected to make landfall on Mexico's Baja Peninsula Monday
Paramount taking over CNN parent Warner Brothers Discovery, with Trump supporter David Ellison in control
Brazilian President Lula da Silva bans online betting ahead of elections, citing debt and addiction crisis
Russian attacks on Ukraine kill four people in Zaporizhia and Sumi over the weekend
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries kill three people in ongoing attacks
Manhunt underway in St. Vincent and Grenadines after shooting kills four people, injures four others
